Description: SpaceBase is a purpose driven consultancy focused on democratizing access to space. Our mission is to address this challenge by catalyzing space industries as a service in emerging and developing countries. Name: The New Zealand Space Health Research Network
Description:
By leveraging New Zealand’s research strengths in medicine, surgery, physiology, biotechnology and bioengineering, pioneering space companies, and advanced space infrastructure, this network aims to foster innovative research, unlock new opportunities, and elevate New Zealand’s position as a major contributor in this emerging field.

Focus and collaborative approach
The network will focus on addressing the unique health challenges of long-term space occupancy while also exploring the benefits these innovations can offer for terrestrial health. The same network aims to coordinate strategic research and foster deep-tech development in space health, seeding new companies that will contribute to the growth and impact of New Zealand’s space sector.

A key commitment of the SHRN is to engage with Māori partners, ensuring their voices help shape the network’s development. Collaboration and engagement are central to the network’s mission, positioning the SHRN to make meaningful contributions to space health and the broader NZ space sector.

Network activities
The Network aims to support the growth and impact of New Zealand’s contribution to the space health field by:
• Coordinating space health initiatives nationwide, to foster synergy and collaboration.
• Integrating Māori perspectives into space health research through a newly established framework.
• Creating pathways for New Zealand students to be involved in the global space industry.
• Engaging with both local and international researchers and commercial stakeholders.
• Facilitating coordinated interactions with major international space research entities (e.g. NASA and ESA).
• Fostering international collaborations and attracting funding for space health project.

Name: Project Kororā - Student Satellite Project
Description:
Project Kororā is Victoria University of Wellington’s first student-run space mission. Our goal is to foster and grow New Zealand’s space community through the development of a 3U CubeSat satellite.

We are a multidisciplinary team of 100+ students from STEM, law, design, and the arts, working together to explore space technology and build real-world skills. Through hands-on projects, workshops, and peer mentorship, Project Kororā provides a platform for students to learn everything from orbit simulation and embedded systems to mechanical design, communications, and space policy.

Our long-term goal is to design and propose a 3U CubeSat equipped with a miniature Hall-effect thruster, developed to operate within the size, power, and thermal constraints of a CubeSat platform. We collaborate with researchers at the Robinson Research Institute and aim to engage with partners across New Zealand’s growing space sector.

The name Kororā comes from New Zealand’s little blue penguin, which is roughly the same size and weight as a 3U CubeSat. The penguin symbolises our mission: to dream boldly and build something extraordinary together, proving that even a flightless bird can inspire a journey to space.

Name: Global Space Enablers Network
Description:
The Global Space Enablers Network (GSEN) is coalition of space enablers and organizations around the world committed to catalyzing and empowering equitable entrepreneurial space ecosystems in developing and emerging countries, to ensure an abundant future in space for everyone.

Founded at the International Astronautical Congress in Milan on 15 October 2024 by 16 organizations from across six continents.  NGO space enabler organizations and individuals worldwide have co-created a decentralized alliance to share best practices, resources, knowledge, etc. We hope to empower local movers directly to catalyze space ecosystems in developing and emerging countries.

Current Initiatives:
1. Knowledge Base - repository of resources to help space enablers catalyze and grow their local ecosystems.
2. Mentorship Program - a pilot to shepherd and mentor new and emerging space communities currently from Costa Rica, Bolivia, Timor Leste, Mexico and Rwanda.

To become a free member org or individual  member (core, project or observer) - sign up at spaceenablers.net/GSEN-Membership/

Name: chroma.space
Description:
chroma.space is an art studio making media performance, mixed reality and art experiences for site-specific locations, galleries, the internet and radio.

In this moment of climate emergency and structural metamorphosis, our mixed reality experiences invite people into alternative collective territories: to hear different stories, see through fresh eyes and experience alternative ways to be together.

chroma.space was founded by Kate Genevieve in 2010. Work shows in theatre settings, art galleries, outdoors and unusual site-specific installations. Name: Women in Space Exploration
Description:
A bold new mission to change the gender paradigm of space.

Women in Space Exploration is on a mission to internationally lead a dramatic and sustained increase in the participation and representation of women at all levels in the space sector.

A registered charity under the New Zealand Charities Act 2005, our purpose is:

To increase the number of girls studying science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) in Aotearoa New Zealand and increase the capability of women working at all levels of Aotearoa New Zealand’s space sector, through 

an all-women space exploration mission 

where inspirational outreach and capability development have equal focus to science and engineering excellence for the mission.

We have a bold 4 point action plan, a detailed phased development plan - and a vision to make dramatic and sustained change to the representation of women in Aotearoa's space sector - through the power of space exploration and a hero team of incredible women space explorers.

Be a part of our bold mission - visit our website to contact us if you want to support our mission or join a phenomenal team dedicated to changing the gender paradigm of space.

Name: Legendary Space
Description:
Vision: To become the most legendary space company in human history—uniting humanity under a golden galaxy of exploration, innovation, and interstellar ambition.

At Legendary Space Ltd, we are more than a company; we are a movement. Our mission is to empower humanity to reach beyond the stars while solving the challenges we face here on Earth. From engineering cutting-edge spacecraft to building sustainable habitats on distant worlds, from mining asteroids to revolutionizing interstellar communication, we are the architects of a future where the universe is humanity’s home—and Earth is just the beginning.

- Beyond the Solar System: Our ambition stretches far beyond Mars or the Moon—we aim for the stars, the galaxies, and the infinite.

Exploration: Venturing into the unknown, driven by curiosity and courage.
R&D: Solving the challenges of tomorrow with today’s breakthroughs.
Stations & Habitats: Creating sustainable homes in orbit, on planets, and beyond.

Name: Astro Ecologies Institute
Description: The Astro Ecologies Institute, founded in 2020, is a research and development initiative exploring eco-social change and communication in the cosmos—on Earth and in outer space. Combining ecological research and astrophysics, the Institute investigates interplanetary communication with creative technologies, embodied practices, and plural knowledge systems. Rooted in ecological principles, Astro Ecologies imagines space futures of resilience and creative connection, shared learning and plurality, while respecting the unique qualities and limits of our home planet in the second space age.

Name: It's not Rocket Science!
Description:
It’s Not Rocket Science! makes STEM education exciting, practical, and accessible through hands-on rocketry, aerospace, and engineering workshops.

Based in Canterbury, we run engaging school sessions, holiday programmes, launch days, and educational experiences that take students beyond worksheets and into real-world problem solving. From building and launching rockets to exploring flight, forces, design, testing, and teamwork, our goal is to turn curiosity into countdowns.

Founded by Simon Willoughby-Martin, an aerospace technician, rocketry educator, and founder of Christchurch Rocketeers, It’s Not Rocket Science! exists to make space and engineering feel less distant — especially for young people who may not otherwise get access to hands-on STEM opportunities.

Because sometimes the best way to learn is to build it, test it, launch it, and ask “what happens if we try that again?”
